hypotheses.reasoning: index-worker was healthy, processing batches with lag under 400ms, until 21:21:33. Then msg-195727 at offset 246773 threw a RangeError (maximum call stack size exceeded) in expandReferences. That looks like a self-referential or cyclic reference in the message. The worker crashes, restarts, picks up again at the same committed offset 246773 and crashes on the same message every time, which is the CrashLoopBackOff. Because the worker never gets past that message, catalog.updates lag climbs to more than 10k, as the search-api warnings show. No other service logged errors. The only earlier warning is a TLS-expiry notice, which is unrelated. The worker comes back as v4.5.8 each time, and I found no deploy near the onset.
The message may carry a cyclic product reference that came from bad catalog data. If so, the real problem is in the data, not the consumer.
The worker runs v4.5.8. If that release changed expandReferences, a new code path could have added the recursion bug. I saw no deploy event before the onset.

verdict.recommendedAction: Move msg-195727 (offset 246773) to a dead-letter queue, or skip it, so index-worker can resume. Then add cycle detection or a depth limit to expandReferences, and catch per-message errors so a bad message gets sent to the DLQ instead of crashing the process. Check the source record behind msg-195727 for a self-referencing product.
